record.original_question: Whenever the natural numbers are finitely colored, must there exist an infinite sequence (y_n)_{n≥1} such that every finite sum a_1 y_1 + a_2 y_2 + ··· + a_k y_k with each coefficient a_i in {1,2} and with a_1 = a_k = 1 has the same color?

evidence.quote: Question 7.1 ([5]). Suppose the natural numbers are coloured with finitely many colours. Must there exist a sequence (yn)∞_{n=1} such that every sum a1y1 + a2y2 + · · · + akyk with ai ∈ {1, 2} for all i and a1 = ak = 1, has the same colour?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{N} = \{1, 2, 3, \dots\}$. Suppose $\mathbb{N}$ is partitioned into finitely many classes (a finite coloring). Must there exist an infinite sequence $(y_n)_{n \geq 1}$ of natural numbers such that the set
$$\Bigl\{\, a_1 y_{n_1} + a_2 y_{n_2} + \cdots + a_k y_{n_k} \,:\, k \geq 1,\ n_1 < n_2 < \cdots < n_k,\ a_i \in \{1,2\},\ a_1 = a_k = 1 \,\Bigr\}$$
is monochromatic (i.e., entirely contained in a single color class)?

Equivalently: in any finite coloring of $\mathbb{N}$, does there exist an infinite sequence $(y_n)$ such that every finite sum $a_1 y_1 + a_2 y_2 + \cdots + a_k y_k$ (taken along an arbitrary increasing index subsequence) with each $a_i \in \{1, 2\}$ and with the first and last coefficients equal to $1$ has the same color?
artifact.status_search_result: This is a restricted-coefficient variant of Hindman's theorem. The full bounded-sum analogue (coefficients in {1,2}) is known to fail or remain open in various forms; the specific version requiring the first and last coefficients to be 1 is a known open problem in partition regularity, included in recent open-problem compilations. Web search reveals ongoing research on bounded-sum Hindman-type theorems but no resolution of this particular question.

status_evidence.title: Open Problems in Partition Regularity
status_evidence.snippet: List of open problems in partition regularity by Hindman, Leader and Strauss.
status_evidence.claim: The question fits within the established list of partition-regularity open problems, none of whose bounded-coefficient Hindman-type variants of this form have been reported as resolved.

status_evidence.title: Effectiveness of Hindman's Theorem for Bounded Sums
status_evidence.snippet: It is not known whether any of these bounded versions of Hindman's Theorem are provable in ACA0... unknown whether HT≤2 has certain properties.
status_evidence.claim: Bounded-sum versions of Hindman's theorem remain open in several formulations.
